scope: Flat portable kernel, consumer linear dispatch, owned array state; no durable storage or external effects.
8/256/4096/65536-byte state; 2/8/32 states and events; accept/reject; 0/1/8/32 intents and count quota refusal.
Rejected profiles return before staging; intent count labels denote configured count only.
Every profile checks initial disposition, rollback/publication, payloads, then final whole state and revision outside timing.
All allocation/deallocation/reallocation/requested-byte counts zero; separate positive control allocates/deallocates 16 bytes.
Quantiles are of per-batch average latency (integer ns); raw elapsed batch samples retained. Throughput uses total elapsed batch time.
Latency includes context, model dispatch/copy, kernel preparation/publication, head/state read and intent drain; instrumentation disabled.
MSRV run is compatibility evidence and unpinned, not a cross-compiler performance comparison.
limitations: Fixed matrix order, short shared-host runs, no confidence intervals or historical equivalent; no regression acceptance or release-wide claim.
Consumer computation/copy cost not yet separately measured; hierarchy, SQLite and end-to-end profiles remain open.
Capacity fixed at 32 across flat profiles, not specialized capacity-zero best case.
